## Git Merge vs Git Rebase

Both integrate changes from one branch into another, but they do it differently.

### Merge

```
main:    A --- B --- C
                      \
feature:               D --- E
```

After `git merge main` on feature:

```
main:    A --- B --- C
                      \       \
feature:               D --- E --- M  (merge commit)
```

- Creates a new "merge commit" (M) that ties the two histories together
- **Preserves the full history** — you can see exactly when branches diverged and rejoined
- Non-destructive: existing commits are never changed

### Rebase

After `git rebase main` on feature:

```
main:    A --- B --- C
                      \
feature:               D' --- E'  (replayed commits)
```

- Replays your commits on top of the target branch — commits get new SHAs (D', E')
- **Rewrites history** to look like you branched off the latest commit
- Result is a linear history with no merge commits

---

## When to use each

**Use merge when:**
- Integrating a completed feature branch into `main` (especially via PR) — preserves the full context of when/why the feature was developed
- Working on a shared branch where others have based work off your commits — rebasing would break their history
- You want an accurate audit trail

**Use rebase when:**
- Updating a local feature branch with upstream changes before submitting a PR — keeps history clean and avoids noisy merge commits
- Cleaning up messy WIP commits before review (`git rebase -i`)
- The branch is **private** (only you use it)

---

## The core tradeoff

| | Merge | Rebase |
|---|---|---|
| History | Truthful, branchy | Clean, linear |
| Safety | Safe on shared branches | **Never rebase shared/public branches** |
| Debuggability | `git log --graph` shows structure | Easier to `git bisect` |
| Noise | Merge commits accumulate | None |

**The golden rule:** never rebase commits that exist on a remote branch others depend on. Rebase rewrites commit SHAs, so anyone with the old commits will have a diverged history — a painful mess to untangle.

A common workflow: rebase locally to stay current with main, then merge (or fast-forward) when the PR lands.
